note: Single source for the branch-separated V-L / V-V pipeline (discovery v5, review v6, scoring v5). Prompts render the checklist and normal-change causes from this file; validators read every code list from it; tests check that the output schemas use the same codes.

v_l_subcategories.presence_count: a required entity/setting is missing; wrong number of instances; an unrequested prominent extra entity; an entity required to stay offscreen is visible; the shot is black or unreadable
v_l_subcategories.attribute: described identity descriptors or properties (age, gender, species, hair, facial hair, clothing, accessories, colors, materials, marks, legible text/numbers/logos, object state such as open/closed, on/off, full/empty), including a described attribute shown on the wrong character
v_l_subcategories.action_state: a described action, motion, pose, gesture or expression is missing, wrong, incomplete, reversed, in the wrong order, or has the wrong start/end state or direction
v_l_subcategories.interaction: the wrong actor/object, or a described holding, touching, using, giving, receiving or contact relation is absent or wrong
v_l_subcategories.spatial_orientation: described positions (left/right, foreground, between, on/in/under), distances, facing or gaze directions
v_l_subcategories.setting_environment: described location type, background elements, time of day, weather, season, lighting or mood
v_l_subcategories.camera_composition: described shot scale, camera angle, viewpoint, framing, focus or camera movement
v_l_subcategories.style_rendering: described rendering style, animation vs live action, color mode, aspect/letterbox
v_l_subcategories.stated_continuity: an explicit sameness/continuity phrase (same, remains, retains, returns to, still, again, unchanged, keeps, familiar, established) is contradicted and no more specific subcategory fits
v_l_subcategories.shot_structure: the required shot transitions or shot plan are not realized (a required cut or continue, a shot's content appearing in another shot's interval, a required new shot repeating the previous one)

within_shot.identity_drift: a person/animal morphs into a different-looking individual (face shape, apparent age, skin tone, facial features)
within_shot.appearance_drift: clothing, hair, accessories, colors or marks change with no visible action
within_shot.action_discontinuity: a character's pose, position or action progress jumps, reverses or restarts between frames without continuous motion (teleport, instant pose change, action reset)
within_shot.object_instability: an object's type, shape, size, color, count, legible text or state changes with no action
within_shot.presence_instability: an entity pops in/out without entry, exit or occlusion (including vanishing for several frames and reappearing); an instance duplicates, splits, or two entities fuse into a hybrid
within_shot.background_drift: background elements or layout change in a way camera motion does not explain
within_shot.physical_integrity: malformed, melting or fused bodies, hands or faces; extra or missing limbs; interpenetration; impossible deformation; a reflection or shadow with no source
within_shot.relation_break: a held object teleports or switches hands; contact, support or relative position changes with no action
within_shot.unintended_cut: the camera setup, composition or setting jumps discontinuously between keyframes of one shot (an unrequested cut), or for an episode-level video the shot change happens deep inside this interval
within_shot.rendering_instability: flicker, color/exposure flash (often only in the first frame), black or blank frames, or a rendering-style switch inside the shot

cross_shot.character_identity: the same character's face, age, gender, skin tone or build differs
cross_shot.character_appearance: the same character's hairstyle/color, facial hair, clothing (garment type, color, pattern, logo, number), accessories, makeup or injuries differ, including attributes that migrate from one character to another
cross_shot.object_identity: the same prop/object/vehicle/animal differs in type, shape, color, markings, legible text or size
cross_shot.setting_background: a recurring location's architecture, wall/floor colors and materials, doors/windows, furniture, vegetation, signage, set dressing or layout differ
cross_shot.environment_lighting: the same continuous scene changes time of day, weather, season, lighting or color grade without a supported cause
cross_shot.rendering_style: photoreal vs animation, 2D vs 3D, or another visual style differs across shots that should share one style
cross_shot.instance_count: a recurring character/object is duplicated, merged with another entity, replaced by a different individual, or two characters who should be distinct look identical or swap looks
cross_shot.state_action_continuity: pose, position, held objects, object states, clothing state or the progress of an ongoing action is incompatible across a boundary or a return, without enough elapsed time or a shown action
cross_shot.spatial_continuity: relative positions, left/right arrangement, screen direction or layout of entities flip or rearrange without a cause, including a layout that contradicts the camera change between the shots
cross_shot.transition_realization: a boundary does not realize its required transition (a required cut that does not happen, or a required continue that is broken)

vv_checklist.title: Camera position and movement inside the shot
vv_checklist.check: For each of frames 0-5 note shot scale, camera angle and camera position/viewpoint. Classify every change: none; smooth movement (pan, tilt, dolly, zoom, handheld drift: the background slides continuously and stays aligned); reframe (gradual change of framing); jump (the background, framing or setting changes discontinuously between two keyframes). A jump inside one shot is an unintended cut unless the text asks for it. Large subject motion against an aligned background is motion, not a cut.

vv_checklist.title: Clothing, hair and accessories of every visible character
vv_checklist.check: For every visible character compare frame by frame each garment (type, color, pattern, logo, neckline, sleeves, layers), hairstyle and hair color, headwear, glasses, jewelry and carried accessories. A change needs a shown action (taking off a jacket, putting on a hat).

vv_checklist.title: Face and identity of every visible character
vv_checklist.check: Compare each face frame by frame: face shape, apparent age, skin tone, eyes and brows, nose, mouth, facial hair, makeup and marks. A different-looking person in the same role is identity drift even when the clothing stays the same. Changes of expression, head turn and lighting are normal.

vv_checklist.title: Actions, poses and bodies
vv_checklist.check: Follow every character's action through frames 0-5: the pose and position must evolve continuously (no teleport, instant pose swap, reversal or restart); hands, limbs and bodies stay intact (no extra or missing limbs, fused or melting bodies, interpenetration).

vv_checklist.title: Objects, held items and contacts
vv_checklist.check: Each visible object keeps its type, shape, size, color, count, text and state; held objects do not teleport or switch hands; contacts and support do not change without an action.

vv_checklist.title: Presence and count
vv_checklist.check: Nobody and nothing pops in or out without entry, exit or occlusion; no instance duplicates, splits or fuses with another.

vv_checklist.title: Background, lighting and rendering inside the shot
vv_checklist.check: Background structures and layout stay the same apart from camera motion; no flicker, exposure flash (check frame 0), black or blank frame, or style switch.

vv_checklist.title: Camera positions across shots
vv_checklist.check: Record the camera position, angle and shot scale of every shot. A new camera position at a cut is normal. For shots that show the same place from a comparable camera position (including a return to an earlier view), the background behind the subject and the layout must match. Across different positions the visible layout (left/right arrangement, screen direction, which side of the room is visible) must be explainable by the camera change.

vv_checklist.title: Faces and identity of recurring characters
vv_checklist.check: For every character visible in two or more shots, including secondary, background, back-view and over-the-shoulder figures, compare face shape, apparent age, skin tone, ethnicity, build and facial features across ALL of its shots, not only one pair. A different face means a different identity even when the clothing matches.

vv_checklist.title: Clothing, hair and accessories of recurring characters
vv_checklist.check: Compare each recurring character's garments (type, color, pattern, logo, neckline, layers), hairstyle (length, texture, color, tied/loose, bangs), facial hair, headwear, glasses, jewelry and makeup across all of its shots, and check that no attribute migrates to another character.

vv_checklist.title: Actions and poses across boundaries and returns
vv_checklist.check: At each boundary compare the last frame of the earlier shot with the first frame of the next shot (and each return to an earlier moment): pose, position, held objects, clothing state and the progress of an ongoing action must be compatible; an action must not reset or repeat unless the shots are separated in time.

vv_checklist.title: Recurring objects
vv_checklist.check: Compare type, shape, color, markings, text and size of every recurring prop, vehicle, animal or furniture item across its shots.

vv_checklist.title: Recurring settings and background elements
vv_checklist.check: For every place that recurs, compare architecture, wall/floor colors and materials, doors and windows, furniture, vegetation, signage and set dressing. Name each changed element (a bench, a sign, a shelf) as an entity, whether or not the text mentions it. Another camera direction explains new elements only if they match the place's style and materials.

vv_checklist.title: Lighting, environment and rendering style
vv_checklist.check: Lighting, time of day, weather, season, color grade and rendering style across shots of the same scene, and across the episode when it should share one style.

vv_checklist.title: Instances
vv_checklist.check: Recurring characters and objects stay distinct and singular: no duplicate, merge, replacement by another individual, look swap between characters.

vv_checklist.title: Spatial layout and screen direction
vv_checklist.check: Relative positions, left/right arrangement and screen direction of recurring entities stay consistent unless an action or the camera change explains them.

vv_checklist.title: Transition realization at every boundary
vv_checklist.check: A required cut must show a clear shot change (new camera setup and/or the next shot's subject); a required continue must continue the same take or moment without a jump or reset. For an interval of one episode video, a cut that lands a fraction of a second late, so that only frame 0 still shows the previous shot, is a timing offset, not a missing cut.

vv_checklist.title: Open-ended sweep
vv_checklist.check: Re-examine every frame for any other obvious or meaningful visual consistency problem, including unusual ones not listed above, and report it with the closest subcategory.

normal_change_causes.camera_motion: a smooth pan, tilt, dolly, zoom or handheld drift inside a shot; the background stays aligned
normal_change_causes.viewpoint_change: a different camera position (at a cut or after a reframe) shows another side or part of the same entity or place, and the elements visible from both positions still match
normal_change_causes.described_action: the text describes the action or change (cause_quote must quote it literally)
normal_change_causes.visible_action: the frames show the action that causes the change (taking something off, picking up, turning, walking)
normal_change_causes.occlusion_or_framing: the entity is occluded, out of frame, cropped, entering or exiting
normal_change_causes.lighting_cause: a visible or described light source, time or weather change explains the lighting difference
normal_change_causes.time_skip: the text or clear visual cues show enough elapsed story time between the shots for this kind of change (never explains a change of face or identity)
normal_change_causes.different_entity: the observations are of different entities or places that are not expected to match
normal_change_causes.required_transition: the change is the required cut itself (a new camera setup at a boundary that requires a cut)
normal_change_causes.cut_timing_offset: an episode-video cut lands slightly late, so only frame 0 of the interval still shows the previous shot
normal_change_causes.image_quality: blur, focus, compression, small size or exposure explains the apparent difference

row_kinds.entity: one contract entity in one shot: its episode-wide description (when the entity is scheduled in the shot) and the shot's single-entity claims about it
row_kinds.relations: the shot's claims that relate two or more entities (positions, contact, interaction)
row_kinds.shot_text: every other explicit requirement of this shot's prompt and of the global prompt that applies to this shot and is not covered by the rows above (catch-all)
row_kinds.transition: the required transition at the boundary into this shot

statuses.satisfied: the frames show content that satisfies the row
statuses.violated: the frames show content that contradicts at least one item of the row (listed in violated_items)
statuses.not_verifiable: the frames cannot decide the row (entity not visible, too small, occluded, ambiguous)
statuses.not_applicable: the row does not apply in this shot (the shot's own text describes the entity differently)

verdicts.confirmed: the core problem of the unit is real and the cited evidence shows it
verdicts.rejected: the core problem itself is false, explained, or belongs to the other branch
verdicts.uncertain: the supplied frames and text cannot reliably decide the core problem

decision_basis_definitions.requirement_violated: V-L confirmed: the quoted text exists, applies to these shots, and a supporting frame shows content contradicting it
decision_basis_definitions.requirement_absent: V-L rejected: the text does not state what the unit claims (the quote is missing or does not mean that)
decision_basis_definitions.requirement_not_applicable: V-L rejected: the requirement exists but does not apply to these shots (the shot's own text describes the entity differently, or the entity is not in the shot)
decision_basis_definitions.requirement_satisfied: V-L rejected: the frames satisfy the quoted words (cite a refuting frame)
decision_basis_definitions.visual_difference_only: V-L rejected: the shot does not conflict with the words and only differs from another shot; that is a V-V question
decision_basis_definitions.inconsistency_confirmed: V-V confirmed: the compared observations should match, they visibly do not, and no normal cause explains the difference
decision_basis_definitions.consistent_in_frames: V-V rejected: the frames show no such difference (cite a refuting frame)
decision_basis_definitions.normal_change: V-V rejected: a normal cause explains the difference (name it in normal_cause)
decision_basis_definitions.not_expected_to_match: V-V rejected: the compared observations are not the same entity, place or moment
decision_basis_definitions.text_violation_only: V-V rejected: the video is consistent with itself and only contradicts the text; that is a V-L question
decision_basis_definitions.not_verifiable: uncertain: name the missing evidence (occlusion, resolution, viewpoint, missing frames)

labels.prompt_bound: the text refers to the entity (a contract entity, a prompt phrase naming it or the role it plays), or it is an intrinsic part (body, face, hair, worn clothing, accessories) of such an entity
labels.prompt_unbound: no global prompt, shot prompt or contract text refers to the entity and it is not part of a referenced entity: the generator introduced it (an unintentional entity)
labels.uncertain: the text could refer to the entity but is too vague to decide (for example "people in the background" for one specific bystander)

basis_types.contract_entity: prompt_bound: the entity is a contract entity (contract_label)
basis_types.prompt_quote: prompt_bound: a literal quote of the prompt or contract names it or its role
basis_types.part_of_entity: prompt_bound: it is an intrinsic part of a prompt-bound entity (part_of)
basis_types.not_in_text: prompt_unbound: no text refers to it
basis_types.ambiguous_text: uncertain: quote the vague text if any and say why it does not decide
